note: Every holding here was retrieved by scripts/works.mjs and its artist field checked against "Edward Hopper". Four of the five sources supply the URL themselves; the Whitney supplies an id, and the path built from it is checked against the museum's own page on every run. A link says a work of this title is held there and can be looked at; it does not say that the ledger row you are reading concerns that copy, and where a museum holds several impressions or versions each is listed separately.

les deux pigeon.why: Leaf 40's descriptor writes the singular and leaf 1's index the plural, of one plate. A slip of the pen, not two works. Both spellings stay as written in the transcription; this only makes the link work from either.

two pigeons.why: The Art Institute catalogues the 1920 plate under an English title where the Met and the Hoppers use the French. Same date, same medium, and the Hoppers' own title is the French one. A judgement, not a slip.

night in the l train.why: The ledger's title for the plate at leaf 30; both the Met and the Art Institute catalogue a 1918 etching as 'Night on the El Train'. The elevated railway is the same railway, but the two titles are not the same words and this is our identification, not theirs.

night hawks.why: Book II leaf 95 heads the canvas « Night Hawks » at 33 x 60, dates it finished 21 January 1942, and books its sale to the Chicago Art Institute on 13 May 1942; the Art Institute catalogues a 1942 oil of 33 1/8 x 60 in. as « Nighthawks », accession 1942.51, and gives its provenance as consigned to Rehn and sold to the museum in 1942. One canvas and one sale, written in two words on the leaf and in one by the museum.
